title: Moons of Mars - Wikipedia
snippet: Two major hypotheses have emerged as to the origin of the moons: The first suggests that they originated from Mars itself, perhaps from a giant impact event suggested to have created the Martian dichotomy and the Borealis Basin. The second suggests that they are captured asteroids.

title: Moons of Mars - NASA Science
snippet: Nov 5, 2024 · Moons of Mars Mars has two moons, Phobos and Deimos. Both are thought to be captured asteroids, or debris from early in the formation of our solar system. Phobos is the larger of Mars' two moons. It orbits Mars three times a day, and is so close to the planet's surface that in some locations on Mars it cannot always be seen.

title: The Moons Of Mars - WorldAtlas
snippet: Phobos and Deimos orbit at vastly different distances from Mars. Phobos is the innermost of the two, orbiting Mars at an average distance of 3,700 miles (6,000 kilometres). title: Moons of Mars - Simple English Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
snippet: The two moons of Mars, Phobos and Deimos, were discovered by the American astronomer Asaph Hall in August 1877. He found them at the United States Naval Observatory in Washington, D.C., [3][4] using a large refracting telescope during a close approach of Mars to Earth.
